name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
summary: A TypeScript framework (npm `agents`) in which every AI agent is a Durable Object: one addressable instance per user or task, with its own SQL state, WebSocket clients, scheduled jobs and MCP tools.
intro: You extend the `Agent` class, which sits on PartyKit’s `partyserver` `Server`, which in turn extends `DurableObject`. Each instance is addressed by a name such as a user ID, ticket number or email address, and the same name always reaches the same instance anywhere on Cloudflare’s network, so there’s no session store to run. `this.setState()` saves state to the instance’s embedded SQLite database and broadcasts it to every connected WebSocket client, which can update it too; `this.sql` queries the database directly. `this.schedule()` takes a delay, a date or a cron string and wakes the agent through Durable Object alarms, methods marked `@callable()` become RPC calls from the browser, and `useAgent()` connects a React app.

The rest is built on top: chat agents with streaming and human-in-the-loop approval, Workflows for steps that run longer than 30 seconds, sub-agents, a Linux sandbox tool backed by Containers, browser tools, and MCP. Its `McpAgent` class (March 2025) was how Cloudflare first hosted remote MCP servers; it is now deprecated in favor of a stateless `createMcpHandler`. Project Think, introduced in April 2026, adds an opinionated harness for long-running agents. The code is MIT-licensed, but it only runs on Cloudflare’s Workers runtime; billing is ordinary Workers and Durable Objects usage.
strengths: One agent instance per user, chat or task, scaling to tens of millions running at once, with up to 1 GB of state each and no external database
Real-time by default: state changes sync to all connected clients over WebSockets, and an idle agent can hibernate and wake on the next request or message
Scheduling, retries, Workflows, sub-agents and MCP come in the box, so long-running and multi-step agents need little extra infrastructure
Model-agnostic: Workers AI by default (no API key in the starter), or OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and others
limits: Tied to Cloudflare: agents are Durable Objects and need the Workers runtime, so the MIT code can’t run on another cloud as is
30 seconds of CPU time per request, message or scheduled task, so heavy or long jobs belong in Workflows or a sandbox
Still pre-1.0 (0.28 on npm) with fast-moving APIs: `McpAgent` is already deprecated and feature-frozen, and the original `agents-sdk` package name has changed
Each instance is single-threaded, so one very busy agent can become a bottleneck; spread work across many instances

story: When Cloudflare built Durable Objects, “Agents” was one of the names proposed for them. The company says it didn’t predict AI agents, but single-threaded, addressable objects with their own storage, alarms and WebSockets turned out to fit them well: an agent needs to remember a conversation, wait on slow model calls, run tasks later and talk to clients in real time.

On February 25, 2025, Rita Kozlov, Sunil Pai and Matt Silverlock released `agents-sdk`, a JavaScript framework for building agents and deploying them on Durable Objects. Even the first release offered real-time client connections, persisted state with `setState` and SQL, scheduled tasks, Workflows, email, web browsing and human-in-the-loop, plus a `useAgent` React hook. A month later `McpAgent` let developers deploy remote MCP servers on Cloudflare.

The package now ships as `agents` from the `cloudflare/agents` repository under the MIT license. In April 2026 Sunil Pai introduced Project Think, “the next generation of the Agents SDK”, with durable execution, sub-agents, sandboxed code execution and persistent sessions for long-running agents, after coding agents like Claude Code and Codex showed what an LLM that can read files and run code can do.

choices.choice: Every agent is a Durable Object
choices.why: The launch post argued that a framework that leaves out durable state, long-running loops and horizontal scale only gets you so far; Durable Objects give each agent a stateful micro-server that scales to tens of millions.
Broadcasting `setState` changes over WebSockets lets a front end and an agent share one source of truth without bespoke sync code.
Agents handle real-time communication and state; Workflows add retries, recovery and waiting for events, so the docs split chat from multi-step background jobs.

timeline.text: `McpAgent` for remote MCP servers on Cloudflare, March 25
Project Think, the next generation of the SDK, on April 15
